html:
The Kingdom of Hungary was a Catholic monarchy in central Europe from the crowning of Stephen I around 1000 until 1946. On the map for 1400 it covers the whole Carpathian Basin, with Croatia attached.

The Magyars settled the Hungarian plain in the 890s, and Stephen's Árpád family ruled for 300 years. After the Árpáds died out in 1301, kings of the Angevin family, Charles I and Louis the Great, made it a major power, rich from gold mines.

In 1400 the king was Sigismund of Luxembourg, who reigned from 1387 to 1437 and later became Holy Roman Emperor. In 1396 he led a crusade against the Ottomans that ended in disaster at the Battle of Nicopolis. Hungary would be the main Christian shield against the Turks for over a century. Its vassals included Wallachia at times. For later centuries see Hungary.
